top3.headline: A ten-person company says its agents ship 108 changes an hour
top3.whyItMatters: Agent fleets can replace review queues with tests and rollback, but it takes heavy token spend.

top3.headline: Hidden Claude Code summaries ate 16% of one team's AI spend
top3.whyItMatters: Agent tools carry default costs you never asked for, so measure where tokens actually go.

top3.headline: Meta puts a personal agent with approvals and audit trails in WhatsApp
top3.whyItMatters: Agents that buy and book are reaching mass consumer apps, with approval gates as the default.

items.title: Codex subagents inherit parent context, hurting clean-context skills
items.takeaway: Pocock found Codex forks the parent's context into most subagents; a fix shipped in his skills repo.
items.soWhat: Review and spec agents need a clean context, so check how your harness spawns them.

items.title: Arizona water fight turns voters against new data centers
items.takeaway: Arizona will lose nearly 30% of its Colorado River water; TSMC's fab uses nearly 5M gallons a day.
items.soWhat: Water is now a siting risk for AI compute, so factor local opposition into capacity plans.

items.title: Palantir's CTO says the AI industry underweights diffusion
items.takeaway: Sankar argues companies focused on the top line adopt AI more successfully; full interview is paywalled.
items.soWhat: Sankar sees adoption as the gap, not models, so point AI at revenue work first.

items.title: Users report OpenAI halves Codex limits on $200 Pro plans
items.takeaway: Per users citing OpenAI's email, from Oct 30 Pro drops from 20x to 10x Plus usage at the same price.
items.soWhat: If teams code on Pro seats, budget for tighter limits or compare other plans now.

related.name: jackcorleone19 on X citing the OpenAI email

items.title: Claude Code status lines took 16% of one team's spend
items.takeaway: Background agent summaries resend full transcripts every 30 seconds; a preload hook turns them off.
items.soWhat: Audit default agent overhead; in one team's measurement it was a sixth of spend.

items.title: Meta launches Muse, a personal agent that acts for you
items.takeaway: Runs tasks on a cloud computer with a browser, via app or WhatsApp; asks before emails or purchases.
items.soWhat: Muse's approvals, audit trail and one-time cards are a useful template for enterprise agents.

items.title: Ten-person Spawn says agents shipped 77,000 changes in 30 days
items.takeaway: $3.1M on tokens last month, no pull requests, hourly deploys, AI judges built from past decisions.
items.soWhat: Spawn trades code review for constant tests and fast rollback; weigh that against your controls.

items.title: Investor says one researcher pretrained a model using agents
items.takeaway: Mamoon Hamid claims agents did almost all engineering on Mirendil-Base in 3.5 months; no technical report.
items.soWhat: If confirmed, model building needs far fewer people; treat it as an unverified claim.
